abstract: We study when positive integer realizations of finite Collatz words can be joined. For each supplied legal word of height at most two on sufficiently late coprime nearcritical rows, and every fixed $1/2<\kappa<1$, we construct $2^{(\kappa/(1-\kappa)+o(1))S}$ positive integer assignments to all $S$ physical positions. Every assigned parity is correct, all values are distinct, and every transition outside a designated set of cuts is genuine, while every designated cut fails. The assignments share a numerical root and weighted total residual, have separation greater than $k/48$, and admit an explicit geometric stability radius. The proof combines a rational gap bound, independent entrance cylinders and a coprime-line union bound. A separate conditional theorem takes an explicit product-law sampling package as input and selects a word whose original longer pieces are individually realizable below $H_2/32$ but cannot join through a positive left entrance up to $H_2^{2-o(1)}$, without a right-center cap. We prove this deduction but do not construct its sampling law. The two constructions share a word and rational profile, not necessarily integer states. The results quantify a gap between simultaneous local integer realizability and global joining. They supply neither arbitrary target-cycle coverage, a numerical asymptotic onset, nor a cycle construction or exclusion. All arguments are symbolic.
